nodes.title: The DFT sum at a root of unity depends only on the frequency modulo the length

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, every $\omega \in \mathbb{C}$, every $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}$ and every natural number $K$,
nodes.title: Even–odd splitting of the DFT sum

nodes.summary: For a natural number $N$, a complex number $\omega$, a sequence $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}$ and a natural number $k$, the unnormalized discrete Fourier sum of length $N$ at frequency $k$ is $\sum_{j=0}^{N-1} \omega^{jk} f(j)$.
nodes.title: Discrete Fourier sum

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a natural number, $\omega \in \mathbb{C}$ a primitive $2^d$-th root of unity, $x_0, \dots, x_{2^d - 1}$ complex numbers and $k < 2^d$. Then the array FFT of the array $(x_0, \dots, x_{2^d - 1})$ with root $\omega$ returns an array $y$ of length $2^d$ whose entry at index $k$ is the discrete Fourier sum $\sum_{j=0}^{2^d - 1} \omega^{jk} x_j$.
nodes.title: The array FFT computes the discrete Fourier transform

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\omega \in R$ and $x$ an array over $R$. The array FFT of $x$ with root $\omega$ returns no result if and only if the length of $x$ is different from $2^d$ for every natural number $d$.
nodes.title: The array FFT rejects exactly the non-powers of two

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $d$ a natural number, $\omega \in R$ and $x$ a vector over $R$ of length $2^d$. Then the array FFT of $x$, viewed as an array, with root $\omega$ returns a result, namely the output of the radix-two FFT of the length-$2^d$ vector $x$ with root $\omega$, viewed as an array.
nodes.title: The array FFT agrees with the vector FFT

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $d$ a natural number, $\omega \in R$ and $x$ a vector over $R$ of length $2^d$. Then the cost $T$ of the array FFT of $x$, viewed as an array, with root $\omega$ satisfies $T + 1 = (7d + 1) \cdot 2^d$.
nodes.title: Exact cost of the array FFT

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $d$ a natural number, $\omega \in R$ and $x$ a vector over $R$ of length $2^d$. Then the cost of the array FFT of $x$, viewed as an array, with root $\omega$ equals the cost of the radix-two FFT of the length-$2^d$ vector $x$ with root $\omega$.
nodes.title: The array FFT costs the same as the vector FFT

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\omega \in R$ and $x$ an array over $R$ of length $n$, and let $d = \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor$ (with $d = 0$ when $n = 0$). If $n = 2^d$, the array FFT runs the radix-two FFT with root $\omega$ on $x$, viewed as a vector of length $2^d$, and returns its output as an array, with the cost of that run. Otherwise it returns no result, at cost $0$; the length check itself is free.
nodes.title: Radix-two FFT on arrays

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\omega \in R$, $m$ a natural number, $q = (q_0, \dots, q_{m-1})$ and $r = (r_0, \dots, r_{m-1})$ vectors over $R$, and $o$ a vector over $R$ of length $2m$. The butterfly loop with root $\omega$ on $q$ and $r$, started from twiddle $1$ and output vector $o$, ends with twiddle $\omega^m$ and an output vector $y$ such that $y_k = q_k + \omega^k r_k$ and $y_{k+m} = q_k - \omega^k r_k$…
nodes.title: Result of the butterfly loop

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $m$ a natural number. For every $\omega \in R$, all vectors $q, r \in R^m$ and every output vector of length $2m$ over $R$, the pass that, starting from twiddle $1$, applies one butterfly for each index $k < m$ in increasing order costs exactly $8m$ charged operations.
nodes.title: Cost of the FFT butterfly pass

nodes.summary: For a commutative ring $R$, an element $\omega \in R$ and vectors $q, r \in R^m$ and $y \in R^{2m}$, the butterfly pass starts from the state $(1, y)$, applies the FFT butterfly with $\omega$, $q$ and $r$ at the indices $k = 0, 1, \dots, m - 1$ in increasing order, and returns the final state; its time cost is the sum of the costs of these $m$ butterflies.
nodes.title: FFT butterfly pass

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\omega \in R$, $m$ a natural number, $q, r$ vectors over $R$ of length $m$, $w \in R$ a twiddle, $o$ an output vector over $R$ of length $2m$, and $k < m$. Then the butterfly step at index $k$ applied to the state $(w, o)$ produces an output vector whose entry at index $k + m$ is $q_k - w r_k$.
nodes.title: Upper write of a butterfly step

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\omega \in R$, $m$ a natural number, $q, r$ vectors over $R$ of length $m$, $w \in R$ a twiddle, $o$ an output vector over $R$ of length $2m$, and $k < m$. Then the butterfly step at index $k$ applied to the state $(w, o)$ produces an output vector whose entry at index $k$ is $q_k + w r_k$.
nodes.title: Lower write of a butterfly step

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\omega \in R$, $m$ a natural number, $q, r$ vectors over $R$ of length $m$, $w \in R$ a twiddle, $o$ an output vector over $R$ of length $2m$, and $k < m$. Then for every index $i < 2m$ with $i \ne k$ and $i \ne k + m$, the butterfly step at index $k$ applied to the state $(w, o)$ produces an output vector whose entry at index $i$ is $o_i$.
nodes.title: A butterfly step leaves other entries unchanged

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $m$ a natural number. For every $\omega \in R$, all vectors $q, r \in R^m$, every current twiddle $w \in R$ and output vector of length $2m$ over $R$, and every index $k < m$, one butterfly step costs exactly $8$ charged operations: two reads, four scalar operations and two writes.
nodes.title: Cost of one FFT butterfly

nodes.summary: For a commutative ring $R$, an element $\omega \in R$, vectors $q, r \in R^m$, a state $(w, y)$ with $w \in R$ and $y \in R^{2m}$, and an index $k < m$, the butterfly at $k$ returns the state $(w \omega, y')$, where $y'$ is obtained from $y$ by setting entry $k$ to $q_k + w r_k$ and entry $k + m$ to $q_k - w r_k$, at a time cost of $8$.
nodes.title: One FFT butterfly

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a field with a star-ring structure, let $\omega \in R$, and let $x$ and $y$ be arrays over $R$. The array circular-convolution procedure with root $\omega$ returns no result on $x$ and $y$ if and only if it is not the case that the length of $x$ is a power of two $2^k$ with $k \ge 0$ and $y$ has the same length as $x$.
nodes.title: Rejection by array circular convolution

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a field with a star-ring structure, let $d$ be a natural number, let $\omega \in R$ be arbitrary, and let $x, y$ be vectors over $R$ of length $2^d$. Then array circular FFT convolution with root $\omega$, run on the arrays underlying $x$ and $y$, succeeds and returns the array underlying the output of vector circular FFT convolution of $x$ and $y$ at size $2^d$ with root $\omega$.
nodes.title: Array circular FFT convolution agrees with the vector version

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a field with a star-ring structure, let $\omega \in R$, and let $x, y$ be arrays over $R$. If array circular FFT convolution with root $\omega$ on $x$ and $y$ returns an array $z$, then $z$ has the same length as $x$.
nodes.title: Output length of array circular FFT convolution

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a field with a star-ring structure, let $d$ be a natural number, let $\omega \in R$, and let $x, y$ be vectors over $R$ of length $2^d$. The time charged by array circular FFT convolution with root $\omega$ on the arrays underlying $x$ and $y$, plus $2$, equals $(21d + 16) \cdot 2^d$.
nodes.title: Exact cost of array circular FFT convolution

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a field with a star-ring structure, let $d$ be a natural number, let $\omega \in R$, and let $x, y$ be vectors over $R$ of length $2^d$. The time charged by array circular FFT convolution with root $\omega$ on the arrays underlying $x$ and $y$ equals the time charged by vector circular FFT convolution of $x$ and $y$ at size $2^d$ with root $\omega$.
nodes.title: Array circular FFT convolution costs the same as the vector version

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a field that is a star ring, $\omega \in R$, and $x, y$ arrays over $R$, where $x$ has length $n$. If $n = 2^d$ for some natural number $d$ and $y$ also has length $n$, the procedure returns the FFT circular convolution of $x$ and $y$ (read as vectors of length $2^d$) with root $\omega$, converted to an array, at the cost of that convolution. nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a field with a star-ring conjugation, let $n = 2^d$, $\omega \in R$ and $x, y \in R^n$. nodes.summary: Let $n = 2^d$ and $x, y \in \mathbb{C}^n$. Then for every $k < n$, entry $k$ of the returned vector equals $\sum_{j \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}} x_j \, y_{k - j}$, with indices taken modulo $n$.
nodes.title: FFT circular convolution with root $e^{-2\pi i/n}$ computes the cyclic convolution

nodes.summary: Let $n = 2^d$ and $x, y \in \mathbb{C}^n$. Run FFT circular convolution of $x$ and $y$ with root $\omega = e^{2\pi i/n}$, the value at $1$ of the standard additive character of $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$. Then for every $k < n$, entry $k$ of the returned vector equals $\sum_{j \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}} x_j \, y_{k - j}$, with indices taken modulo $n$.
nodes.title: FFT circular convolution with root $e^{2\pi i/n}$ computes the cyclic convolution

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a field with a star-ring structure, let $d$ be a natural number, let $\omega \in R$, and let $x$ and $y$ be vectors of length $2^d$ over $R$. The cost charged by circular convolution of $x$ and $y$ with root $\omega$, plus $2$, equals $(21d + 16) \cdot 2^d$.

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a field with a star-ring structure, let $d$ be a natural number, let $\omega \in R$, and let $x$ and $y$ be vectors of length $2^d$ over $R$. nodes.summary: For all vectors $x, y \in \mathbb{C}^n$ and every natural number $k \ge 2n$, the coefficient of $X^k$ in the product of the polynomials of $x$ and $y$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Coefficients of a product beyond twice the length vanish

nodes.summary: Let $x, y \in \mathbb{C}^n$, and set $x_i = y_i = 0$ for $i \ge n$. For every natural number $k$, the coefficient of $X^k$ in the product of the polynomials of $x$ and $y$ is $\sum_{j=0}^{k} x_j y_{k-j}$.
nodes.title: Coefficients of a product of vector polynomials

nodes.summary: For every natural number $d$ and all vectors $x, y \in \mathbb{C}^{2^d}$, the coefficient of $X^{2 \cdot 2^d - 1}$ in the product of the polynomials of $x$ and $y$ is $0$.
nodes.title: The last coefficient of a doubled-length product vanishes

nodes.summary: The polynomial of a vector $x = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}) \in \mathbb{C}^n$ is $\sum_{j=0}^{n-1} x_j X^j \in \mathbb{C}[X]$, the complex polynomial whose coefficient of $X^j$ is $x_j$ for $j < n$ and $0$ for $j \ge n$.
nodes.title: Polynomial of a coefficient vector

Let $e, o \in R^{2^d}$ be the even- and odd-indexed subsequences of $x$ returned by the FFT split, and let $E$ and $O$ be the vectors returned by the radix-two FFT of depth $d$ with root $\omega \cdot \omega$ on $e$ and on $o$. nodes.title: High half of the FFT butterfly recurrence

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $d$ a natural number, $\omega \in R$ and $x \in R^{2^{d+1}}$, with entries indexed from $0$. Let $e, o \in R^{2^d}$ be the even- and odd-indexed subsequences of $x$ returned by the FFT split, and let $E$ and $O$ be the vectors returned by the radix-two FFT of depth $d$ with root $\omega \cdot \omega$ on $e$ and on $o$. Then for every $k < 2^d$, entry $k$ of the vector returned by the…
nodes.title: Low half of the FFT butterfly recurrence

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. For every $\omega \in R$ and every vector $x \in R^{2^0}$, the vector returned by the radix-two FFT of depth $0$ with root $\omega$ on $x$ is $x$ itself.
nodes.title: The FFT of depth zero returns its input

nodes.summary: For a type with a multiplication, a scalar $c$ and a vector $x = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ of length $n$ over it, this costed computation returns $(c x_0, \dots, c x_{n-1})$ and charges $3n$ operations: one read, one multiplication and one write per entry.
nodes.title: Charged entrywise scaling

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a type, $m$ a natural number and $x = (x_0, \dots, x_{2m-1})$ a vector of length $2m$ over $R$. For every $k < m$, entry $k$ of the first (even) vector returned by the FFT split of $x$ is $x_{2k}$.
nodes.title: The FFT split extracts the even-indexed entries

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a type, $m$ a natural number and $x = (x_0, \dots, x_{2m-1})$ a vector of length $2m$ over $R$. For every $k < m$, entry $k$ of the second (odd) vector returned by the FFT split of $x$ is $x_{2k+1}$.
nodes.title: The FFT split extracts the odd-indexed entries

nodes.summary: For every natural number $m$ and every vector $x$ of length $2m$, splitting $x$ into its even-indexed and its odd-indexed subsequences costs exactly $4m$ charged operations: two reads and two writes for each of the $m$ even/odd pairs.
nodes.title: Cost of the FFT even/odd split

nodes.summary: For a commutative ring $R$, a natural number $m$ and a vector $x = (x_0, \dots, x_{2m-1}) \in R^{2m}$, the split returns the pair of vectors $(x_0, x_2, \dots, x_{2m-2})$ and $(x_1, x_3, \dots, x_{2m-1})$ in $R^m$ of the entries of $x$ at even and at odd indices, in order, at a time cost of $4m$ (the charged reads and writes).
nodes.title: Even–odd split for the FFT

Run the radix-two FFT on $x$ with sample root $\omega = e^{-2\pi i/n}$, the value at $-1$ of the standard additive character of $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$. Run the radix-two FFT on $x$ with sample root $\omega = e^{2\pi i/n}$, the value at $1$ of the standard additive character of $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$. nodes.title: The radix-two FFT with root $e^{2\pi i/n}$, divided by $n$, computes the inverse DFT

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. For every natural number $d$, every $\omega \in R$ and every vector $x$ over $R$ of length $n = 2^d$, the radix-two FFT of $x$ with root $\omega$ costs $T$ charged operations, where $T + 1 = (7 \log_2 n + 1) \cdot n$.
nodes.title: Exact cost of the radix-two FFT in terms of the input length

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. For every natural number $d$, every $\omega \in R$ and every vector $x \in R^{2^d}$, the radix-two FFT of $x$ with root $\omega$ costs $T$ charged operations, where $T + 1 = (7d + 1) \cdot 2^d$; that is, $T = (7d + 1) \cdot 2^d - 1$.
nodes.title: Exact cost of the radix-two FFT

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. For every natural number $d$, every $\omega \in R$ and every vector $x \in R^{2^d}$, the radix-two FFT of $x$ with root $\omega$ costs at most $8 \cdot 2^d \cdot d$ charged operations, that is, at most eight per entry per recursion level.
nodes.title: Cost bound for the radix-two FFT

nodes.summary: For a commutative ring $R$, a natural number $d$, an element $\omega \in R$ and a vector $x \in R^{2^d}$, the FFT of $x$ with root $\omega$ is defined by recursion on $d$. For $d = 0$ it returns $x$ at cost $0$. For $d + 1$ it splits $x$ into its even- and odd-indexed subvectors $e, o \in R^{2^d}$ (cost $4 \cdot 2^d$), computes $\omega^2$ (cost $1$), computes the FFTs $q$ of $e$ and $r$ of $o$ with root $\omega^2$,…
nodes.title: Radix-two fast Fourier transform

For every $k < N$, entry $k$ of the output of the inverse FFT procedure on $x$ with root $\omega$ equals $N^{-1}$ times the discrete Fourier sum of length $N$ with root $\overline{\omega}$ at frequency $k$ of the sequence $j \mapsto x_j$ (set to $0$ for $j \ge N$), that is,…
nodes.title: Correctness of the inverse FFT

nodes.summary: Let $N = 2^d$ and let $\omega = e^{-2\pi i/N}$, the value at $-1$ of the standard additive character of $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$. For every $x \in \mathbb{C}^N$, running the FFT procedure on $x$ with root $\omega$ and then the inverse FFT procedure on its output with root $\omega$ returns $x$.
nodes.title: Inverse FFT after FFT is the identity at the negative-sign root

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a natural number, $N = 2^d$ and $\omega = e^{2\pi i/N}$. For every vector $x \in \mathbb{C}^N$, running the radix-two FFT with root $\omega$ on $x$ and then the inverse FFT with root $\omega$ on its output returns $x$.
nodes.title: Inverse FFT after FFT at the positive root is the identity

nodes.summary: Let $N = 2^d$, let $\omega \in \mathbb{C}$ be a primitive $N$-th root of unity and let $x \in \mathbb{C}^N$. The output of the inverse FFT procedure on $x$ with root $\omega$ is the output of the FFT procedure on $x$ with root $\overline{\omega}$ with every entry multiplied by $N^{-1}$.
nodes.title: The inverse FFT is a normalized FFT at the conjugate root

nodes.summary: Let $N = 2^d$ and $x \in \mathbb{C}^N$, and run the inverse FFT procedure on $x$ with root $e^{-2\pi i/N}$, the value at $-1$ of the standard additive character of $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$. nodes.title: Inverse FFT at the negative-sign root computes the inverse DFT

nodes.summary: Let $N = 2^d$ and $x \in \mathbb{C}^N$, and run the inverse FFT procedure on $x$ with root $e^{2\pi i/N}$, the value at $1$ of the standard additive character of $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$. For every $k < N$, entry $k$ of its output equals $N^{-1}$ times the canonical discrete Fourier transform of the function on $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$ sending the class of $j < N$ to $x_j$, evaluated at the class of $k$; that is,…
nodes.title: Inverse FFT at the positive-sign root computes the normalized forward DFT

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a field with a star ring structure, let $d$ be a natural number, $N = 2^d$, $\omega \in R$ arbitrary and $x \in R^N$. The number $T$ of operations charged by the inverse FFT procedure on $x$ with root $\omega$ satisfies $T + 1 = (7d + 10) \cdot 2^d + 1$, equivalently $T = (7d + 10) \cdot 2^d$.
nodes.title: Exact operation count of the inverse FFT

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a field with a star ring structure, let $d$ be a natural number, $N = 2^d$, $\omega \in R$ arbitrary and $x \in R^N$. The number of operations charged by the inverse FFT procedure on $x$ with root $\omega$ is at most $8 \cdot 2^d \cdot d + 9 \cdot 2^d + 1$.
nodes.title: Operation bound for the inverse FFT

Analysis

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
